claim: Antibody class switching is a feature of the adaptive immune system which enables diversification of the effector properties of antibodies.
source: Antibody class switching is a feature of the adaptive immune system which enables diversification of the effector properties of antibodies.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the adaptive immune system.

claim: Class switching is essential for mounting a protective response to pathogens.
source: Even though class switching is essential for mounting a protective response to pathogens, the in vivo patterns and lineage characteristics of antibody class switching have remained uncharacterized in living humans.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about immune function.

claim: The in vivo patterns and lineage characteristics of antibody class switching have remained uncharacterized in living humans prior to this study.
source: Even though class switching is essential for mounting a protective response to pathogens, the in vivo patterns and lineage characteristics of antibody class switching have remained uncharacterized in living humans.
evidence: This statement describes the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The study comprehensively measured the landscape of antibody class switching in human adult twins using antibody repertoire sequencing.
source: Here we comprehensively measured the landscape of antibody class switching in human adult twins using antibody repertoire sequencing.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The map identifies how antibodies of every class are created.
source: The map identifies how antibodies of every class are created and delineates a two-tiered hierarchy of class switch pathways.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on the data collected.

claim: The study delineates a two-tiered hierarchy of class switch pathways.
source: The map identifies how antibodies of every class are created and delineates a two-tiered hierarchy of class switch pathways.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on the data collected.

claim: Closely related B cells often switch to the same class.
source: Using somatic hypermutations as a molecular clock, we discovered that closely related B cells often switch to the same class, but lose coherence as somatic mutations accumulate.
evidence: This is a finding from the study using somatic mutations as a molecular clock.

claim: Closely related B cells lose coherence in class switching as somatic mutations accumulate.
source: Using somatic hypermutations as a molecular clock, we discovered that closely related B cells often switch to the same class, but lose coherence as somatic mutations accumulate.
evidence: This is a finding from the study using somatic mutations as a molecular clock.

claim: Correlations between closely related cells exist when purified B cells class switch in vitro.
source: Such correlations between closely related cells exist when purified B cells class switch in vitro, suggesting that class switch recombination is directed toward specific isotypes by a cell-autonomous imprinted state.
evidence: This is a finding from in vitro experiments with purified B cells.

claim: Class switch recombination is directed toward specific isotypes by a cell-autonomous imprinted state.
source: Such correlations between closely related cells exist when purified B cells class switch in vitro, suggesting that class switch recombination is directed toward specific isotypes by a cell-autonomous imprinted state.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the in vitro experimental results.

claim: Different classes of antibodies with distinct Fc domains mediate specialized effector functions, including activation of complement, phagocytosis, cytotoxicity, and release of inflammatory mediators.
source: Different classes of antibodies with distinct Fc domains mediate specialized effector functions, including activation of complement, phagocytosis, cytotoxicity, and release of inflammatory mediators (Kindt et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to established literature.

claim: Dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in allergic hypersensitivity.
source: Conversely, dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in autoimmune diseases, including allergic hypersensitivity (Sugai et al., 2003), rheumatoid arthritis (Humby et al., 2009), systemic lupus erythematosus (Bubier et al., 2009; Mietzner et al., 2008), IgG4-related disease (Stone et al., 2012), and hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome (Minegishi, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in rheumatoid arthritis.
source: Conversely, dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in autoimmune diseases, including allergic hypersensitivity (Sugai et al., 2003), rheumatoid arthritis (Humby et al., 2009), systemic lupus erythematosus (Bubier et al., 2009; Mietzner et al., 2008), IgG4-related disease (Stone et al., 2012), and hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome (Minegishi, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in systemic lupus erythematosus.
source: Conversely, dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in autoimmune diseases, including allergic hypersensitivity (Sugai et al., 2003), rheumatoid arthritis (Humby et al., 2009), systemic lupus erythematosus (Bubier et al., 2009; Mietzner et al., 2008), IgG4-related disease (Stone et al., 2012), and hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome (Minegishi, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in IgG4-related disease.
source: Conversely, dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in autoimmune diseases, including allergic hypersensitivity (Sugai et al., 2003), rheumatoid arthritis (Humby et al., 2009), systemic lupus erythematosus (Bubier et al., 2009; Mietzner et al., 2008), IgG4-related disease (Stone et al., 2012), and hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome (Minegishi, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome.
source: Conversely, dysregulation of antibody class switching has been implicated in autoimmune diseases, including allergic hypersensitivity (Sugai et al., 2003), rheumatoid arthritis (Humby et al., 2009), systemic lupus erythematosus (Bubier et al., 2009; Mietzner et al., 2008), IgG4-related disease (Stone et al., 2012), and hyperimmunoglobulin E syndrome (Minegishi, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Class switching occurs during germinal center maturation and is linked to cell division and somatic hypermutation.
source: Class switching occurs during germinal center maturation and is linked to cell division and somatic hypermutation (Hodgkin et al., 1996; Liu et al., 1996; Tangye et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: After antigen encounter, IgM+ and IgD+ naïve B cells can switch to expression of activated classes IgG, IgA, and IgE via genomic recombination of the immunoglobulin heavy chain constant region locus.
source: After antigen encounter, IgM+ and IgD+ naïve B cells can switch to expression of activated classes IgG, IgA, and IgE via genomic recombination of the immunoglobulin heavy chain constant region locus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about B cell biology.

claim: Much of current knowledge about the mechanisms of class switching is derived from the analysis of B cells induced to undergo class switch recombination (CSR) in vitro.
source: Much of current knowledge about the mechanisms of class switching is derived from the analysis of B cells induced to undergo class switch recombination (CSR) in vitro.
evidence: This describes the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The patterns of antibody class switching in the natural setting within a living organism have remained largely uncharacterized.
source: However, the patterns of antibody class switching in the natural setting within a living organism have remained largely uncharacterized.
evidence: This describes the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Cytokine signals, such as CD40 ligand, IL-4, IFNγ, and TGFβ, induce CSR and can direct switching toward specific classes in vitro.
source: Cytokine signals, such as CD40 ligand, IL-4, IFNγ, and TGFβ, induce CSR and can direct switching toward specific classes in vitro (Stavnezer, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Cytokine signals likely originate from cognate Th cells and dendritic cells in vivo.
source: These signals likely originate from cognate Th cells and dendritic cells in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge of immune cell interactions.

claim: Cytokine stimulation induces transcription and splicing of 'germline' transcripts from the switch region of the particular IGHC locus that is participating in CSR.
source: Cytokine stimulation induces transcription and splicing of 'germline' transcripts from the switch region of the particular IGHC locus that is participating in CSR (Lorenz et al., 1995; Stavnezer-Nordgren and Sirlin, 1986).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Switch regions accumulate histone modifications that are associated with open chromatin conformations and high DNA accessibility.
source: These switch regions accumulate histone modifications that are associated with open chromatin conformations and high DNA accessibility (Jeevan-Raj et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Epigenetic control of switch region accessibility directs CSR toward specific classes.
source: Together, these experiments suggest a model in which epigenetic control of switch region accessibility directs CSR toward specific classes (Alt et al., 1986; Stavnezer-Nordgren and Sirlin, 1986; Vaidyanathan and Chaudhuri, 2015).
evidence: This is a model supported by citations to published research.

claim: The study mapped the landscape of human antibody class switching using high-throughput immune repertoire sequencing.
source: In this study, we mapped the landscape of human antibody class switching using high-throughput immune repertoire sequencing (Boyd et al., 2009; Weinstein et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study, with citations to the sequencing method.

claim: Immune repertoire sequencing has previously yielded insights into how the immune system responds to pathogen challenge and vaccination.
source: This method has previously yielded insights into how the immune system responds to pathogen challenge and vaccination (Jackson et al., 2014a; Jiang et al., 2013; Parameswaran et al., 2013; Racanelli et al., 2011; Vollmers et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2014) and changes with age (Jiang et al., 2011, 2013; Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: Immune repertoire sequencing has previously yielded insights into how the immune system changes with age.
source: This method has previously yielded insights into how the immune system responds to pathogen challenge and vaccination (Jackson et al., 2014a; Jiang et al., 2013; Parameswaran et al., 2013; Racanelli et al., 2011; Vollmers et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2014) and changes with age (Jiang et al., 2011, 2013; Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The study developed an approach for reconstructing clonal histories of antibody lineages, including class switching events.
source: We developed an approach for reconstructing clonal histories of antibody lineages, including class switching events.
evidence: This describes a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The study measured antibody class switching within clonal lineages across the entire repertoire in vivo in a cohort of healthy human twins.
source: We used this method to measure antibody class switching within clonal lineages across the entire repertoire in vivo in a cohort of healthy human twins.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The comprehensive map identifies how antibodies of every class are created.
source: This comprehensive map identifies how antibodies of every class are created.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: Analysis of class switching events within clonal lineages uncovered signatures of the cellular decision processes that direct CSR toward specific isotypes.
source: Our analysis of class switching events within clonal lineages uncovered signatures of the cellular decision processes that direct CSR toward specific isotypes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study.

claim: The study conducted immune repertoire sequencing of immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) genes of 22 healthy young adult human twins, including 9 pairs of identical twins and 2 pairs of fraternal twins.
source: To investigate human antibody class switching in vivo, we conducted immune repertoire sequencing of immunoglobulin heavy chain (IGH) genes of 22 healthy young adult human twins, including 9 pairs of identical twins and 2 pairs of fraternal twins.
evidence: This describes the study cohort and experimental design.

claim: Sequencing libraries were prepared of a ~430–480 bp fragment of the IGH gene using total RNA from peripheral blood B cells.
source: Sequencing libraries were prepared of a ~430–480 bp fragment of the IGH gene using total RNA from peripheral blood B cells drawn from each subject.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: Libraries were sequenced with 300 bp paired-end reads on the Illumina Miseq platform.
source: Libraries were sequenced with 300 bp paired-end reads on the Illumina Miseq platform.
evidence: This describes the sequencing methodology.

claim: Individual RNA molecules were labeled with unique molecular barcodes during library preparation, enabling highly accurate measurement of genetic diversity by using a consensus read approach to correct PCR and sequencing errors.
source: Individual RNA molecules were labeled with unique molecular barcodes during library preparation, enabling highly accurate measurement of genetic diversity by using a consensus read approach to correct PCR and sequencing errors (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Vollmers et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes the methodology with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: On average, ~261,000 raw reads were obtained from each individual at each time point, representing ~154,000 unique sequences.
source: On average, ~261,000 raw reads were obtained from each individual at each time point, representing ~154,000 unique sequences (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the sequencing data, with reference to a figure.

claim: Sequencing reads covered ~100 bp of the constant region, making it possible to determine antibody class and resolve subclasses (IgG1, IgG2, IgG3, IgG4, IgA1, and IgA2) with high accuracy.
source: Sequencing reads covered ~100 bp of the constant region, making it possible to determine antibody class and resolve subclasses (IgG1, IgG2, IgG3, IgG4, IgA1, and IgA2) with high accuracy.
evidence: This describes the capability of the sequencing approach.

claim: Across individuals, the most abundant class was IgM (75%), followed by IgG1 (10%) and IgA1 (8%).
source: Across individuals, the most abundant class was IgM (75%), followed by IgG1 (10%) and IgA1 (8%) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and Table 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data, with reference to a figure and table.

claim: For 14 of 22 subjects, the measurement was repeated 28 days after the initial sample as a biological replicate.
source: For 14 of 22 subjects, the measurement was repeated 28 days after the initial sample as a biological replicate (Bio. Rep.).
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: The class distributions are essentially the same across replicates in nearly every subject.
source: As expected, the class distributions are essentially the same across replicates in nearly every subject (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: V gene usage is highly similar across biological replicates.
source: Furthermore, V gene usage is highly similar across biological replicates (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: After activation by specific antigen, naïve B cells proliferate and undergo somatic hypermutation and class switching.
source: After activation by specific antigen, naïve B cells proliferate and undergo somatic hypermutation and class switching.
evidence: This is established knowledge about B cell biology.

claim: This process gives rise to a clonally related lineage composed of antibody IGH sequences of distinct classes that also differ in the variable region due to accumulation of somatic mutations.
source: This process gives rise to a clonally related lineage composed of antibody IGH sequences of distinct classes that also differ in the variable region due to accumulation of somatic mutations.
evidence: This is established knowledge about B cell biology.

claim: The study developed an approach for reconstructing the clonal history of antibody lineages by using the information contained in the accumulation of somatic mutations as a molecular clock.
source: To study class switching after B cell activation, we developed an approach for reconstructing the clonal history of antibody lineages by using the information contained in the accumulation of somatic mutations as a molecular clock, much as ribosomal 16S sequences are used to study the evolutionary relationships of life on earth.
evidence: This describes a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: Sequences belonging to the same clonal lineage were identified as those sharing a variable (V) and joining (J) gene combination, CDR3 length, and ≥95% sequence identity in both the CDR3 and the rest of the variable region with at least one other member of the lineage.
source: We identified sequences belonging to the same clonal lineage as those sharing a variable (V) and joining (J) gene combination, CDR3 length, and ≥95% sequence identity in both the CDR3 and the rest of the variable region with at least one other member of the lineage (Figure 1—figure supplement 5, Figure 2—figure supplement 7, and Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the methodology for identifying clonal lineages, with references to figures.

claim: A minimum evolution tree was reconstructed for each clonal lineage by conducting a multiple sequence alignment of all sequences in the lineage and then identifying a minimum spanning tree which includes all the sequences and minimizes the total number of mutations across the tree.
source: We reconstructed a minimum evolution tree for each clonal lineage by conducting a multiple sequence alignment of all sequences in the lineage and then identifying a minimum spanning tree which includes all the sequences and minimizes the total number of mutations across the tree.
evidence: This describes the methodology for reconstructing lineage trees.

claim: CSR occurs through a genomic rearrangement of the IGH constant region locus that brings the gene segment encoding the new constant region closer to the VDJ locus.
source: CSR occurs through a genomic rearrangement of the IGH constant region locus that brings the gene segment encoding the new constant region closer to the VDJ locus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of CSR.

claim: Gene segments between the old and new constant regions are looped out and deleted during CSR.
source: Gene segments between the old and new constant regions are looped out and deleted (Iwasato et al., 1990; Schwedler et al., 1990; Yoshida et al., 1990).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Class switches are irreversible and must proceed from upstream classes to downstream classes, according to the order of the IGH constant region loci on the chromosome.
source: Therefore, class switches are irreversible and must proceed from upstream classes to downstream classes, according to the order of the IGH constant region loci on the chromosome, which is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.
evidence: This is an inference based on the mechanism of CSR, with reference to a figure.

claim: The constraint that class switches must proceed from upstream to downstream classes was incorporated into the algorithm for clonal history reconstruction.
source: This provides a constraint on ancestry that we incorporated into our algorithm for clonal history reconstruction: for a sequence belonging to a given class, only sequences of upstream classes can be ancestors.
evidence: This describes a methodological decision in the study.

claim: The lineage trees are rooted on the germline sequence of the V and J gene combination shared by the lineage.
source: The lineage trees are rooted on the germline sequence of the V and J gene combination shared by the lineage.
evidence: This describes the methodology for constructing lineage trees.

claim: Somatic mutations accumulate as one moves from the germline sequence toward the leaves of the trees.
source: As expected, somatic mutations accumulate as one moves from the germline sequence toward the leaves of the trees (Figure 1—figure supplement 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: PCR and sequencing errors rarely give rise to sequences having different classes and therefore contribute minimally to error in measuring class switching.
source: We note that PCR and sequencing errors rarely give rise to sequences having different classes and therefore contribute minimally to error in measuring class switching.
evidence: This is an inference about the quality of the data.

claim: PCR and sequencing errors terminate branches of the tree and do not affect analysis of mutation accumulation and correlations in class switching patterns.
source: Because these errors terminate branches of the tree, they also do not affect our analysis of mutation accumulation and correlations in class switching patterns.
evidence: This is an inference about the impact of errors on the analysis.

claim: The tree reconstruction approach enables direct measurement of class switching events in clonal lineages which are supported by observed sequences without the need to infer mutations or ancestral isotype states.
source: Unlike previous approaches (Barak et al., 2008), our tree reconstruction approach enables direct measurement of class switching events in clonal lineages which are supported by observed sequences without the need to infer mutations or ancestral isotype states.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the methodology compared to previous approaches, with a citation.

claim: The inference process is challenging and indirect due to the complex mutational spectrum of somatic hypermutation.
source: The inference process is challenging and indirect due to the complex mutational spectrum of somatic hypermutation.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges of alternative approaches.

claim: The ~154,000 unique sequences from each subject belonged to ~34,000 distinct clonal lineages on average.
source: The ~154,000 unique sequences from each subject belonged to ~34,000 distinct clonal lineages on average (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: On average across all subjects, each sequence displays 99.2% identity in the VDJ variable region to its parent.
source: On average across all subjects, each sequence displays 99.2% identity in the VDJ variable region to its parent (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B), suggesting that the repertoire has been sampled deeply enough to enable accurate, high-resolution reconstruction of lineage history, since most pairs of sequences are separated by at most a few sites of hypermutation.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The repertoire has been sampled deeply enough to enable accurate, high-resolution reconstruction of lineage history.
source: On average across all subjects, each sequence displays 99.2% identity in the VDJ variable region to its parent (Figure 1—figure supplement 6B), suggesting that the repertoire has been sampled deeply enough to enable accurate, high-resolution reconstruction of lineage history, since most pairs of sequences are separated by at most a few sites of hypermutation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the high sequence identity between parent-child pairs.

claim: The study devised an algorithm that traverses the reconstructed tree for each lineage and counts switches between classes from ancestor to child.
source: We devised an algorithm that traverses the reconstructed tree for each lineage and counts switches between classes from ancestor to child.
evidence: This describes the methodology for measuring class switching.

claim: The relative frequency of switching between every pair of classes was calculated.
source: We then calculated the relative frequency of switching between every pair of classes.
evidence: This describes the methodology for analyzing class switching.

claim: In total ~142,000 class switch events were observed and contributed to this data set.
source: In total ~142,000 class switch events were observed and contributed to this data set.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: The study detected ~35,000 pairs of sequences sharing identical VDJ sequences but having different classes, as indicated by differing constant region sequences.
source: To characterize the accuracy of this approach, we note that we detected ~35,000 pairs of sequences sharing identical VDJ sequences but having different classes, as indicated by differing constant region sequences.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data analysis.

claim: Every molecule has a unique barcode associated with it, proving that sequences with identical VDJ but different classes are not due to PCR recombination artifacts.
source: Since every molecule has a unique barcode associated with it, we are able to prove that these sequences are not due to PCR recombination artifacts (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Sequence pairs with identical VDJ but different classes arose from CSR without intervening hypermutation events.
source: These sequence pairs arose from CSR without intervening hypermutation events and enable analysis of class switching rates on a subset of the data without the need for lineage identification or tree construction.
evidence: This is an inference about the origin of these sequence pairs.

claim: When analysis was conducted using only sequences with identical VDJ but different classes, the patterns of class switching correlate extremely well with the landscape measured across the entire repertoire.
source: When we conducted our analysis using only these sequences, we found that the patterns of class switching correlate extremely well with the landscape measured across the entire repertoire, showing that the full lineage tree approach faithfully measures class switching patterns (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C; Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with references to figures and a table.

claim: Patterns of class switching measured using only sequences that inherited all of the germline mutations from their immediate ancestor are highly similar to those measured using the full lineage tree approach.
source: We further confirmed that the patterns of class switching measured using only sequences that inherited all of the germline mutations from their immediate ancestor are highly similar to those measured using the full lineage tree approach (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), indicating that artifacts arising from imperfect sampling of ancestral sequences have not distorted our measurement.
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Patterns of class switching measured using only sequences supported by at least three sequencing reads are highly similar to those measured using the full lineage tree approach.
source: In addition, patterns of class switching measured using only sequences supported by at least three sequencing reads are highly similar to those measured using the full lineage tree approach, suggesting that PCR and sequencing error have not substantially distorted our measurement (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Patterns of class switching could not simply be explained by random switching in proportion to class abundance.
source: Finally, we confirmed that patterns of class switching could not simply be explained by random switching in proportion to class abundance. After shuffling the classes of parent-child sequence pairs, the hierarchical class switching patterns that we observed vanished (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The landscape asymptotes rapidly to the observed one as read sampling depth is increased.
source: To confirm that we measured the antibody repertoire with sufficient depth to accurately characterize the class switching landscape, we performed rarefaction analysis using data from five subjects. This analysis revealed that the landscape asymptotes rapidly to the observed one as read sampling depth is increased (Figure 2—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a finding from rarefaction analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The fraction of class switches that occur via an intermediate saturates as read sampling depth is increased.
source: Since class switch intermediates that are missing from the data could contribute to error in our measurement, we performed additional rarefaction analysis to show that the fraction of class switches that occur via an intermediate also saturates as read sampling depth is increased (Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a finding from rarefaction analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: In ~1500 sequences detected in both biological replicates of the same subject, in 99.9% of cases the class of the ancestor sequence was the same in both samples.
source: As further validation, we examined ~1500 sequences that were detected in both biological replicates of the same subject and found that in 99.9% of cases the class of the ancestor sequence was the same in both samples, indicating that the presence or absence of switch intermediates is reliably detected.
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis.

claim: The dominant class switch pathway leads from IgM/IgD to IgG1 or IgA1.
source: The dominant class switch pathway leads from IgM/IgD to IgG1 or IgA1.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the class switching landscape analysis.

claim: IgM switched most commonly to IgG1, IgA1, and IgG2, which together account for ~85% of switches from IgM.
source: Specifically, IgM switched most commonly to IgG1, IgA1, and IgG2, which together account for ~85% of switches from IgM.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the class switching landscape analysis.

claim: Direct switches from IgM to downstream classes (IgG4, IgE, or IgA2) were rare (~14%).
source: Direct switches from IgM to downstream classes (IgG4, IgE, or IgA2) were rare (~14%).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the class switching landscape analysis.

claim: Downstream classes are predominantly produced via indirect switches.
source: Instead, downstream classes are predominantly produced via indirect switches (Figure 2B), most often through IgG1 or IgA1 in a secondary hierarchy of pathways.
evidence: This is a finding from the class switching landscape analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: IgG1 frequently switched to IgA1 or IgG2, which together account for ~92% of switches from IgG1.
source: For example, IgG1 frequently switched to IgA1 or IgG2, which together account for ~92% of switches from IgG1, but rarely switched directly to IgG4 or IgA2.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the class switching landscape analysis.

claim: IgG1 rarely switched directly to IgG4 or IgA2.
source: For example, IgG1 frequently switched to IgA1 or IgG2, which together account for ~92% of switches from IgG1, but rarely switched directly to IgG4 or IgA2.
evidence: This is a finding from the class switching landscape analysis.

claim: Most IgA2 was produced by subsequent switches from IgA1 or IgG2 (~65%), instead of directly from IgG1.
source: Most IgA2 was produced by subsequent switches from IgA1 or IgG2 (~65%), instead of directly from IgG1.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the class switching landscape analysis.

claim: IgG3 is more likely to switch to IgG1/2 (~87%) rather than IgA1/2.
source: We also saw that IgG3 is more likely to switch to IgG1/2 (~87%) rather than IgA1/2, suggesting that IgG3 lies along a pathway for specific generation of IgG antibodies.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the class switching landscape analysis.

claim: IgG3 lies along a pathway for specific generation of IgG antibodies.
source: We also saw that IgG3 is more likely to switch to IgG1/2 (~87%) rather than IgA1/2, suggesting that IgG3 lies along a pathway for specific generation of IgG antibodies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the class switching patterns observed.

claim: The class switching landscape and the penetrance of direct and indirect switches were highly reproducible across the biological replicates, which were separated by 28 days.
source: The class switching landscape and the penetrance of direct and indirect switches were highly reproducible across the biological replicates, which were separated by 28 days (Figure 2C,Figure 2—figure supplement 8B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 9), confirming the robustness of our measurements and suggesting that the landscape is a temporally invariant feature of the healthy human immune system.
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with references to figures.

claim: The landscape is a temporally invariant feature of the healthy human immune system.
source: The class switching landscape and the penetrance of direct and indirect switches were highly reproducible across the biological replicates, which were separated by 28 days (Figure 2C,Figure 2—figure supplement 8B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 9), confirming the robustness of our measurements and suggesting that the landscape is a temporally invariant feature of the healthy human immune system.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reproducibility of the landscape across time points.

claim: The landscapes of individual subjects are broadly similar.
source: Next, we examined how the landscape of class switching varies between individuals. The landscapes of individual subjects are broadly similar (Figure 2—figure supplements 9 and 10), and the dominant usage of several major switch pathways is conserved across all subjects (Figure 2—figure supplement 9D).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with references to figures.

claim: The dominant usage of several major switch pathways is conserved across all subjects.
source: Next, we examined how the landscape of class switching varies between individuals. The landscapes of individual subjects are broadly similar (Figure 2—figure supplements 9 and 10), and the dominant usage of several major switch pathways is conserved across all subjects (Figure 2—figure supplement 9D).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The magnitude of variation between subjects is similar to variation between biological replicates of the same subject.
source: This similarity is also apparent when measured by the Jensen-Shannon distance, which reveals that the magnitude of variation between subjects is similar to variation between biological replicates of the same subject (Figure 2—figure supplement 9A and B).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: Healthy young adults share a broadly conserved landscape of antibody class switching.
source: We conclude that healthy young adults share a broadly conserved landscape of antibody class switching.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the similarity of landscapes across subjects.

claim: The class switching patterns of identical twins are no better correlated than pairs of unrelated individuals.
source: We also asked whether class switching landscapes were more similar among identical twins compared to unrelated individuals. We found that the class switching patterns of identical twins are no better correlated than pairs of unrelated individuals (Figure 2—figure supplement 9A–C), suggesting that the regulation of CSR involves substantial environmental or stochastic influences, as has been found in many other parameters of the immune system (Brodin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with references to figures and a citation.

claim: The regulation of CSR involves substantial environmental or stochastic influences.
source: We also asked whether class switching landscapes were more similar among identical twins compared to unrelated individuals. We found that the class switching patterns of identical twins are no better correlated than pairs of unrelated individuals (Figure 2—figure supplement 9A–C), suggesting that the regulation of CSR involves substantial environmental or stochastic influences, as has been found in many other parameters of the immune system (Brodin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of correlation between identical twins, with a citation to supporting literature.

claim: Naïve classes (IgM or IgD) accumulated significantly more mutations before undergoing CSR to activated classes (IgG, IgA, or IgE), in comparison with CSR between activated classes.
source: We found that naïve classes (IgM or IgD) accumulated significantly more mutations before undergoing CSR to activated classes (IgG, IgA, or IgE), in comparison with CSR between activated classes.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of somatic mutations prior to CSR.

claim: Among IgM/IgD sequences, the average number of mutations accumulated in the variable region prior to CSR is 4.1 ± 6.7 (mean ± s.d.).
source: Among IgM/IgD sequences, the average number of mutations accumulated in the variable region prior to CSR is 4.1 ± 6.7 (mean ± s.d.).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the data analysis.

claim: Only 2.5 ± 4.3 mutations accumulate in sequences of activated classes prior to further CSR.
source: In contrast, only 2.5 ± 4.3 mutations accumulate in sequences of activated classes prior to further CSR (Figure 2—figure supplement 11B and C; p = 1.8 × 10–45 and 1.3 × 10–12 for Samples and Bio. Rep. respectively; Mann-Whitney U test, two-sided).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the data analysis, with reference to figures and statistical test results.

claim: The distributions of mutations accumulated prior to CSR were well fit by an exponential distribution.
source: We found that the distributions of mutations accumulated prior to CSR were well fit by an exponential distribution, suggesting that CSR is a memory-less process with respect to somatic mutation and allowing us to estimate rates of CSR (Figure 2—figure supplement 11E).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: CSR is a memory-less process with respect to somatic mutation.
source: We found that the distributions of mutations accumulated prior to CSR were well fit by an exponential distribution, suggesting that CSR is a memory-less process with respect to somatic mutation and allowing us to estimate rates of CSR (Figure 2—figure supplement 11E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the exponential distribution fit.

claim: The rate constants of class switching from IgM/IgD to activated classes were ~0.37 mutation-1.
source: We found that the rate constants of class switching from IgM/IgD to activated classes were ~0.37 mutation-1 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The rate constants of switching between activated classes were ~0.60 mutation-1.
source: By contrast, the rate constants of switching between activated classes were ~0.60 mutation-1 (p < 1.5 × 10–4; Mann-Whitney U test, two-sided).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the data analysis, with statistical test results.

claim: These patterns of CSR rates were robustly observed across biological replicates.
source: These patterns were robustly observed across biological replicates (Figure 2—figure supplement 11D).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Measurements of the number of mutations accumulated in IgM sequences prior to class switching are likely an underestimate.
source: Because class switching can be initiated from mutated IgM memory cells for which we may have failed to detect naïve progenitors, our measurements of the number of mutations accumulated in IgM sequences prior to class switching are likely an underestimate, supporting an argument for differences in the rate of CSR between naïve and activated classes.
evidence: This is an inference about potential limitations of the measurement.

claim: Activated B cells which have already undergone class switching tend to rapidly undergo further class switching, as measured by the clock of somatic hypermutation.
source: Thus, our results suggest that activated B cells which have already undergone class switching tend to rapidly undergo further class switching, as measured by the clock of somatic hypermutation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the rate constant analysis.

claim: Closely related cells made highly concordant class switch decisions.
source: We discovered that closely related cells made highly concordant class switch decisions (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of class switch fates among related cells, with reference to a figure.

claim: The most closely related cells, separated by ≤2 mutations from their common progenitor, had a very significant tendency to switch to the same class, in contrast to unrelated pairs of cells.
source: The most closely related cells, separated by ≤2 mutations from their common progenitor, had a very significant tendency to switch to the same class, in contrast to unrelated pairs of cells which were obtained by shuffling (p values ranging from 6 × 10–5 to 1.1 × 10–186; Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure and statistical test results.

claim: The concordance in class switch fates dissipated as somatic mutations accumulated, becoming indistinguishable from unrelated cells after ~10 somatic mutations.
source: When we examined pairs of cells that were less closely related (as measured by mutations from their common progenitor), we found that the concordance in class switch fates dissipated as somatic mutations accumulated, becoming indistinguishable from unrelated cells after ~10 somatic mutations (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with references to figures.

claim: Closely related cells exhibit probability distributions that are strongly biased toward the same class switch fate, and the bias dissipates as somatic mutations accumulate.
source: These findings were corroborated by examining the probability distributions of class switch fate conditioned upon the fate of a closely related cell: closely related cells exhibit probability distributions that are strongly biased toward the same class switch fate, and the bias dissipates as somatic mutations accumulate (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Mutational distances (i.e. branch lengths) are not associated with particular switching events.
source: Importantly, we found that mutational distances (i.e. branch lengths) are not associated with particular switching events (Figure 3—figure supplement 6), and that mutational distances among related sequences are not correlated (Figure 3—figure supplement 7), indicating that correlations in switch fate are not due to differential sampling of lineages.
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with references to figures.

claim: Mutational distances among related sequences are not correlated.
source: Importantly, we found that mutational distances (i.e. branch lengths) are not associated with particular switching events (Figure 3—figure supplement 6), and that mutational distances among related sequences are not correlated (Figure 3—figure supplement 7), indicating that correlations in switch fate are not due to differential sampling of lineages.
evidence: This is a finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Correlations in switch fate are not due to differential sampling of lineages.
source: Importantly, we found that mutational distances (i.e. branch lengths) are not associated with particular switching events (Figure 3—figure supplement 6), and that mutational distances among related sequences are not correlated (Figure 3—figure supplement 7), indicating that correlations in switch fate are not due to differential sampling of lineages.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of correlation in mutational distances.

claim: Class switch decisions are coordinated within clonal lineages of B cells in living humans.
source: These findings demonstrate that class switch decisions are coordinated within clonal lineages of B cells in living humans and that this coordination dissipates at large genealogical distances within a lineage.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings about concordance in class switch fates.

claim: Coordination of class switch decisions dissipates at large genealogical distances within a lineage.
source: These findings demonstrate that class switch decisions are coordinated within clonal lineages of B cells in living humans and that this coordination dissipates at large genealogical distances within a lineage.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings about concordance in class switch fates.

claim: CD19+ IgM+ B cells were purified from whole blood and cultured in the presence of multimeric CD40 ligand (CD40L), IL-4, and IL-10 for 8 days.
source: To discriminate between these models and test whether cellular interactions are necessary to generate correlations between class switch fates of sibling cells, we measured the class switch behavior of purified primary human B cells stimulated with cytokines in culture. We purified CD19+ IgM+ B cells from whole blood (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A) and cultured them in the presence of multimeric CD40 ligand (CD40L), IL-4, and IL-10 for 8 days, then prepared sequencing libraries of the IGH locus.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the in vitro experiment, with reference to a figure.

claim: The purified B cells were 99.6% CD19+.
source: The purified B cells were 99.6% CD19+ (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), and sequencing of the IgM+ cells used to initiate the culture revealed that 97% of the sequences were IgM/IgD (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the in vitro experiment, with reference to figures.

claim: Sequencing of the IgM+ cells used to initiate the culture revealed that 97% of the sequences were IgM/IgD.
source: The purified B cells were 99.6% CD19+ (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), and sequencing of the IgM+ cells used to initiate the culture revealed that 97% of the sequences were IgM/IgD (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the in vitro experiment, with reference to a figure.

claim: During culture, the cells proliferated and underwent class switching to IgG1, IgG2, IgG3, and IgA1.
source: During culture, the cells proliferated and underwent class switching to IgG1, IgG2, IgG3, and IgA1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a finding from the in vitro experiment, with reference to a figure.

claim: After reconstructing the histories of clonal lineages, ~1900 pairs of IgM/IgD sequences sharing a common progenitor that subsequently underwent class switching were identified.
source: After reconstructing the histories of clonal lineages, we identified ~1900 pairs of IgM/IgD sequences sharing a common progenitor that subsequently underwent class switching.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the in vitro experiment.

claim: In vitro, the concordance between the class switch fates of the most closely related cells was as evident as in vivo.
source: In vitro, the concordance between the class switch fates of the most closely related cells was as evident as in vivo (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the in vitro experiment, with reference to a figure.

claim: Closely related sequences separated from a common progenitor by ≤2 substitutions exhibited a highly significant tendency to switch to the same class in vitro, in comparison with unrelated sequences.
source: Closely related sequences separated from a common progenitor by ≤2 substitutions exhibited a highly significant tendency to switch to the same class, in comparison with unrelated sequences (p values ranging from 5 × 10–4 to 5 × 10–28).
evidence: This is a finding from the in vitro experiment, with statistical test results.

claim: No pairs of sequences sharing a common progenitor that subsequently underwent class switching were detected in the IgM+ B cell populations that initiated the culture.
source: Importantly, no pairs of sequences sharing a common progenitor that subsequently underwent class switching were detected in the IgM+ B cell populations that initiated the culture, confirming that imperfect IgM+ B cell purification cannot account for the class switches detected after culturing.
evidence: This is a finding from the in vitro experiment.

claim: Coordination of class switch decisions in clonal lineages of B cells is not dependent upon the in vivo environment and interactions with cognate cells.
source: These results demonstrate that coordination of class switch decisions in clonal lineages of B cells is not dependent upon the in vivo environment and interactions with cognate cells, but rather seems to be an autonomous property of purified B cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro experimental results.

claim: Coordination of class switch decisions seems to be an autonomous property of purified B cells.
source: These results demonstrate that coordination of class switch decisions in clonal lineages of B cells is not dependent upon the in vivo environment and interactions with cognate cells, but rather seems to be an autonomous property of purified B cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro experimental results.

claim: CSR is directed toward specific isotypes by an imprinted state, which is transmitted from a common progenitor to sister cells.
source: This finding suggests that CSR is directed toward specific isotypes by an imprinted state, which is transmitted from a common progenitor to sister cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the in vitro experimental results.

claim: The findings provide a comprehensive map of the patterns of antibody class switching in humans.
source: Our findings provide a comprehensive map of the patterns of antibody class switching in humans.

claim: Pathways of CSR are organized into two tiers: (1) naïve classes (IgM/IgD) switch predominantly to proximal classes such as IgG3, IgG1, or IgA1, and (2) proximal classes may subsequently switch to distal classes, such as IgG2, IgG4, or IgA2.
source: The data reveal that pathways of CSR are organized into two tiers: (1) naïve classes (IgM/IgD) switch predominantly to proximal classes such as IgG3, IgG1, or IgA1, and (2) proximal classes may subsequently switch to distal classes, such as IgG2, IgG4, or IgA2.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary finding about the hierarchy of class switching.

claim: IgG1 and IgA1 seem to be central intermediates linking naïve to distal classes.
source: IgG1 and IgA1 seem to be central intermediates linking naïve to distal classes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the class switching patterns observed.

claim: This hierarchy mirrors the linear geometry of the IGH constant region loci on chromosome 14, suggesting that chromosomal structure or topology influences CSR.
source: This hierarchy mirrors the linear geometry of the IGH constant region loci on chromosome 14, suggesting that chromosomal structure or topology influences CSR.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the class switching patterns in relation to chromosomal structure.

claim: Mouse B cells stimulated in vitro with CD40L and IL-4 switched to IgG1 with high frequency after three divisions, while switching to the downstream classes IgE and IgG2a increased after five or six divisions.
source: Consistent with this, previous studies which showed that mouse B cells stimulated in vitro with CD40L and IL-4 switched to IgG1 with high frequency after three divisions, while switching to the downstream classes IgE and IgG2a increased after five or six divisions (Hasbold et al., 1998; Hodgkin et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: A previous study on human populations reported increasing levels of point mutation in progressively further downstream IgG subclasses, supporting sequential class switching.
source: A previous study on human populations reported increasing levels of point mutation in progressively further downstream IgG subclasses, supporting sequential class switching (Jackson et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: A previous study suggested the existence of a preferential switch pathway from IgG2 to IgA2 based on evidence of stronger antigen-driven selection in IgA2 than IgA1 sequences.
source: This study also suggested the existence of a preferential switch pathway from IgG2 to IgA2 based on evidence of stronger antigen-driven selection in IgA2 than IgA1 sequences, which is consistent with our results.
evidence: This is supported by reference to a previous study.

claim: Examination of clonal histories of B cell lineages with mixed isotypes provides more direct evidence for sequential class switching and the existence of dominant class switch pathways.
source: Our examination of clonal histories of B cell lineages with mixed isotypes provides more direct evidence for sequential class switching and the existence of dominant class switch pathways.
evidence: This is a statement about the contribution of the study compared to previous work.

claim: Measurements of switch rates can be affected by undersampling of ancestors, especially for switches between rare classes, such as IgE and IgG4.
source: While our lineage reconstruction approach circumvents the difficulties associated with ancestral inference and probabilistic models of class switching, one limitation is that measurements of switch rates can be affected by undersampling of ancestors, especially for switches between rare classes, such as IgE and IgG4.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the methodology.

claim: The undersampling rate was estimated to range from 0.1% to 5% depending on the subject.
source: We have estimated this undersampling rate by using a Chapman estimator to gauge the total number of each isotype in circulation compared to the number we detected, and found results ranging from 0.1% to 5% depending on the subject, which does not affect any of the conclusions of this work.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of undersampling.

claim: The study identifies ten class switch transitions which to the authors' knowledge have not been previously identified.
source: Prior to this work a limited number of class transitions had been observed in human samples. Our data identifies ten transitions which to our knowledge have not been previously identified (Table 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, with reference to a table.

claim: With the possible exception of IgE, any transition which is permitted to happen by the geometry of the immunoglobulin locus is observed in healthy human samples.
source: In conjunction with other published results, it appears that, with the possible exception of IgE, any transition which is permitted to happen by the geometry of the immunoglobulin locus is observed in healthy human samples.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the study's findings and published literature.

claim: The machinery underlying CSR is intrinsically stochastic, and biological regulation enforces probabilistic preferences, rather than strict rules in switch behavior.
source: This finding supports the view that the machinery underlying CSR is intrinsically stochastic, and that biological regulation enforces probabilistic preferences, rather than strict rules in switch behavior.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings about the diversity of observed transitions.

claim: The broad contours of the class switching landscape appear to be conserved across individuals.
source: The broad contours of the class switching landscape appear to be conserved across individuals, but there is variation between individuals that likely reflects differences in the history of immune activation and environmental exposure.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of landscapes across individuals.

claim: Variation between individuals in class switching likely reflects differences in the history of immune activation and environmental exposure.
source: The broad contours of the class switching landscape appear to be conserved across individuals, but there is variation between individuals that likely reflects differences in the history of immune activation and environmental exposure.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the variation observed between individuals.

claim: Identical twins did not exhibit identical class switching landscapes, indicating that class switching is driven largely by non-heritable factors.
source: Importantly, identical twins did not exhibit identical class switching landscapes, indicating that class switching is driven largely by non-heritable factors, which likely include exposure to pathogens or other microbes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of identical twins.

claim: Non-heritable factors driving class switching likely include exposure to pathogens or other microbes.
source: Importantly, identical twins did not exhibit identical class switching landscapes, indicating that class switching is driven largely by non-heritable factors, which likely include exposure to pathogens or other microbes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the non-heritable factors.

claim: Previous studies of identical twins have suggested that genetic background controls features of the antibody repertoire, such as IGHV, IGHD, and IGHJ gene use, and CDR3 length.
source: Previous studies of identical twins have suggested that genetic background controls features of the antibody repertoire, such as IGHV, IGHD, and IGHJ gene use, and CDR3 length (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Studies examining other components of the immune system have indicated that non-heritable factors dominantly influence most features of serological and cellular responses, including serum protein abundances and cell populations.
source: On the other hand, studies examining other components of the immune system have indicated that non-heritable factors dominantly influence most features of serological and cellular responses, including serum protein abundances and cell populations (Brodin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to published research.

claim: Variation between humans in the class composition of the antibody repertoire is predominantly driven by the ability of the immune system to adapt to environmental stimuli, rather than genetic predisposition.
source: Our findings suggest that variation between human in the class composition of the antibody repertoire is predominantly driven by the ability of the immune system to adapt to environmental stimuli, rather than genetic predisposition.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings about identical twins.

claim: Unique landscapes of antibody class switching in identical twins likely arise from the unpredictable stimulation of B cell clones and different exposure to many microbes over the course of a lifetime.
source: Unique landscapes of antibody class switching in identical twins likely arise from the unpredictable stimulation of B cell clones and different exposure to many microbes over the course of a lifetime.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the variation observed in identical twins.

claim: The measurement of the conserved class switching landscape of healthy, young adult humans provides a reference for comparison against individuals with altered immune states, such as autoimmunity or chronic infection.
source: Our measurement of the conserved class switching landscape of healthy, young adult humans provides a reference for comparison against individuals with altered immune states, such as autoimmunity or chronic infection.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential application of the findings.

claim: The work demonstrates how somatic mutations can be exploited as a molecular clock to reconstruct the genealogies of cells and characterize the dynamics of cell state.
source: Our work demonstrates how somatic mutations can be exploited as a molecular clock to reconstruct the genealogies of cells and characterize the dynamics of cell state.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: Strong correlations between the class switch fates of closely related B cells were uncovered which have undergone maturation in the natural context in living humans.
source: We have uncovered strong correlations between the class switch fates of closely related B cells which have undergone maturation in the natural context in living humans.
evidence: This is a summary of a primary finding.

claim: Correlations in class switch fates appear to decay on a timescale of ~10 somatic mutations.
source: These correlations appear to decay on a timescale of ~10 somatic mutations.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the analysis of correlations.

claim: Correlations between closely related cells are also generated during in vitro culture of purified B cell populations in the presence of cytokines that induce class switching.
source: Such correlations between closely related cells are also generated during in vitro culture of purified B cell populations in the presence of cytokines that induce class switching, demonstrating that the correlations are an autonomous property of purified B cells and that the in vivo environment is not necessary to create them.
evidence: This is a finding from the in vitro experiments.

claim: Correlations in class switch fate are an autonomous property of purified B cells and the in vivo environment is not necessary to create them.
source: Such correlations between closely related cells are also generated during in vitro culture of purified B cell populations in the presence of cytokines that induce class switching, demonstrating that the correlations are an autonomous property of purified B cells and that the in vivo environment is not necessary to create them.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro experimental results.

claim: Cytokine signals driving CSR in vivo likely originate from cognate T helper cells and dendritic cells in localized intercellular niches.
source: Although cytokine signals driving CSR in vivo likely originate from cognate T helper cells and dendritic cells in localized intercellular niches, our experiments show that correlations in class switch fate between sibling cells cannot simply be attributed to exposure to common signals due to co-occupancy of the same niche.
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge of immune cell interactions.

claim: Correlations in class switch fate between sibling cells cannot simply be attributed to exposure to common signals due to co-occupancy of the same niche.
source: Although cytokine signals driving CSR in vivo likely originate from cognate T helper cells and dendritic cells in localized intercellular niches, our experiments show that correlations in class switch fate between sibling cells cannot simply be attributed to exposure to common signals due to co-occupancy of the same niche.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the in vitro experimental results.

claim: The mode of regulation of class switching contrasts with stem cell maintenance and differentiation in the mammalian lung, which are regulated by signaling from parent/progenitor cells to daughter cells in localized niches.
source: This mode of regulation contrasts with stem cell maintenance and differentiation in the mammalian lung, which are regulated by signaling from parent/progenitor cells to daughter cells in localized niches (Pardo-Saganta et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison to another biological system, with a citation.

claim: The correlations observed in vitro were not quite as strong as those seen in vivo, suggesting that cellular interactions in the natural context might enhance sibling correlations in class switch fates.
source: We note that the correlations that we observed in vitro were not quite as strong as those seen in vivo, suggesting that cellular interactions in the natural context might enhance sibling correlations in class switch fates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the difference between in vivo and in vitro results.

source: We note that in our culture experiments the starting populations were heterogeneous and included both naïve and memory B cells, leaving the lineage characteristics of class switching within these compartments to be examined in future work.

claim: The data suggest a model where CSR is directed toward specific classes by a transient epigenetic state, which is transmitted from parent cells to daughter cells and relaxes on a timescale of ~10 somatic mutations.
source: Our data suggest a model where CSR is directed toward specific classes by a transient epigenetic state, which is transmitted from parent cells to daughter cells and relaxes on a timescale of ~10 somatic mutations.

source: Consistent with this, directed CSR is thought to be regulated via cytokine-activated transcription at specific IGHC loci, which targets the region for modification by activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID).

claim: Germline transcription of IGHC genes is associated with histone modifications that increase DNA accessibility.
source: Germline transcription of IGHC genes is associated with histone modifications that increase DNA accessibility (Jeevan-Raj et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2009), and germline IGHC transcripts can form RNA-DNA hybrids with genomic DNA, exposing ssDNA to AID attack (Reaban and Griffin, 1990; Reaban et al., 1994; Yu et al., 2003).

claim: Germline IGHC transcripts can form RNA-DNA hybrids with genomic DNA, exposing ssDNA to AID attack.
source: Germline transcription of IGHC genes is associated with histone modifications that increase DNA accessibility (Jeevan-Raj et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2009), and germline IGHC transcripts can form RNA-DNA hybrids with genomic DNA, exposing ssDNA to AID attack (Reaban and Griffin, 1990; Reaban et al., 1994; Yu et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

source: Using single-cell transcriptomics, we have found that single B cells stimulated to class switch in vitro often predominantly express germline transcripts from a single IGHC locus (F. Horns, unpublished data).

source: We propose that inheritance during mitosis of germline transcripts and chromatin state in the IGHC locus, including perhaps histone modifications influencing DNA accessibility, is a mechanism that generates correlations in the class switch fates of sister cells.

source: Together with recent studies of mammalian (Spencer et al., 2009) and bacterial cells in culture (Hormoz et al., 2015), our work suggests that phenotypic correlations between sister cells due to shared inheritance are widespread.

source: We predict that such correlations often will be detected when genealogical relationships between individual cells can be resolved.

source: We propose that inheritance of epigenetic state provides a mechanism for orchestrating cellular behavior without the need for signaling.
